flow_ref: User story (not in a flow deck, OCMS has none)
code_summary: ocmsadminui pages/NoticeSearch/hook/useSearchParams.tsx, pages/Notice/hook/useStagePermissions.tsx (stage gate for editing a notice, not mention outcome); ocmsadminapi workflows/notice_creation/core/helpers/SuspensionBaseHelper (suspension stage check). ocmsadminprivateapi, ocmseserviceapi, ocmseserviceui, thirdpartyapi: no mention outcome code
note: Sheet status: Demo paid (50% of 75%); demo_remark empty. The story asks OCMS to validate whether the searched notice may receive a mention outcome (for example processing stage) and to prompt when it does not apply. No such validation exists because the mention outcome feature itself does not exist (see OCMS25.1). The UI stage gate for editing a notice and the suspension stage check are different mechanisms and are not credited as mention-outcome validation. No maintenance ticket changes the verdict. The pre-defined conditions beyond the processing stage example are not given in the story.
recommendation: Not claimable as built. Only the generic notice search is Sebagian; mention outcome validation and prompt do not exist in code.

steps.step: Officer searches for a notice by notice number in OCMS (precondition for recording a mention outcome)
steps.detail: A generic notice search exists in the staff portal: the notice_no form value is read (useSearchParams.tsx:167) and added to the list of notices searched (useSearchParams.tsx:258). It is a generic search, not a screen dedicated to recording mention outcomes, so Sebagian. There is no outcome-related search criterion (the words dnata/adjourn/withdraw appear nowhere in the six repos except the message at useStagePermissions.tsx:86).

steps.step: OCMS validates whether the notice may receive a mention outcome based on pre-defined conditions (for example processing stage)
steps.detail: There is no mention-outcome applicability validation. The nearest thing is a UI stage gate for editing a notice (useStagePermissions.tsx:31-55, EDITABLE/NON_EDITABLE stage lists) and the message 'Notice has been submitted to State Court. Please apply DNATA and perform an EMCONs to edit the notice' (useStagePermissions.tsx:86). That decides whether a notice can be edited, not whether a mention outcome can be recorded, so it is not credited. In the API, the 'Notice is under Court processing' stage check (SuspensionBaseHelper.java:209-210) belongs to suspensions, not mention outcomes. Tried synonyms mention outcome, dnata, adjourn/adjournment, withdraw/withdrawal, discharge, hearing, postpone, acquit across all six repos (java, ts/tsx, properties, sql; ocmsadminapi, ocmsadminprivateapi, ocmsadminui, ocmseserviceapi, ocmseserviceui, thirdpartyapi) in both UI and API layers. Only relevant hits: the UI message at useStagePermissions.tsx:86 telling the officer to 'apply DNATA' with no DNATA function behind it; the type Icourtmention.d.ts:1-33 (field mention_outcome) is TypeScript only and unused; /v1/courtmention is in api-authorization.properties:23 but there is no courtmention controller/entity in ocmsadminapi and the UI never calls it.

steps.step: OCMS prompts the officer when the searched notice is not applicable
steps.detail: There is no mention-outcome prompt. The ModalAlert in useStagePermissions.tsx:82-100 is only used to block notice editing with the DNATA/EMCONs message, not for mention-outcome validation.
